Get the rows of a lookup table

Source: R/dimension.R
gcd_dimension.Rd

Returns one of the platform's six lookup tables, the reference lists every dataset's codes point to. They hold much more than names, and the API never adds it to dataset rows:

  • "districts": district name, former names, type, Census id, county, address, coordinates, active flag.

  • "schools": school name, former names, level, grade span, county, NCES id, address, phone, website, coordinates, locale (city, suburb, town, rural), charter and active flags.

  • "counties": the 159 county names (without "County").

  • "tracts": 2020 Census tracts with county, land area and population.

  • "block_groups": 2020 block groups with tract, county, land area, population, housing units and households.

  • "demographics": each demographic group's label and category.

Use it to analyze results by locale, map schools, or browse what exists ("every school in Fulton County"). Unfiltered tables are cached for the R session.

Usage

gcd_dimension(
  name,
  ...,
  district = NULL,
  school = NULL,
  county = NULL,
  q = NULL,
  columns = NULL,
  n_max = Inf
)

Arguments

name

The lookup table: "districts", "schools", "counties", "tracts", "block_groups" or "demographics".

...

Named filters on the table's key, enum and boolean columns, and county_fips, district_code or tract_geoid where the table has them. Each takes a vector (values are OR'd; filters are AND'd), for example active = TRUE, district_type = "state_charter" or county_fips = "13121".

district, school, county

Places by name, matched exactly against current and former names (ignoring case, accents and a trailing "County") and turned into codes. Character vectors; default NULL. Each applies only to tables with that code column.

q

A single string: partial text search over the table's name columns, ignoring case and accents (q = "eastside"). Unlike the name arguments, it matches part of a name and returns every hit, so it is the tool for browsing. Default NULL.

columns

A character vector of columns to return. Default NULL: all.

n_max

The most rows to return. Default Inf: all.

Value

A tibble ordered by the table's primary key, one row per district, school, county, tract, block group or demographic group, typed from the table's schema: codes (district_code, school_code, county_fips, tract_geoid, block_group_geoid, demographic) and text columns are character, coordinates and areas double, counts and directory_year integer, active and charter logical. See gcd_columns() for each table's columns.

Joining schools

School codes repeat across districts, so join on district_code and school_code together:

schools <- gcd_dimension("schools",
                         columns = c("district_code", "school_code", "locale"))
grad |>
  dplyr::left_join(schools, by = c("district_code", "school_code"))

See also

gcd_columns() for a table's column dictionary; gcd_rows(), whose results carry these tables' names beside their codes.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # interactive()
gcd_dimension("counties")
gcd_dimension("schools", county = "Fulton", active = TRUE)
gcd_dimension("districts", district_type = "state_charter")
gcd_dimension("schools", q = "eastside",
              columns = c("district_code", "school_code", "school_name"))
}
